label: Meals per life
note: Average over his last five lives in each of three runs, after ten lives of practice. The pass mark, set before the run, is five small meals a life.

label: Lives in which he eats
note: Share of 47 exam lives in which he ate at least once, with no curriculum. None of the six curricula tried did better.

label: Length of a life
note: His last five lives against an untrained copy of himself. To pass he must outlive that twin by a margin fixed before the run. Without food no life can pass 600 seconds.

label: What living adds
note: Seconds of life his practice bought him over the untrained twin. A negative number means training made him worse.

label: Finds food sooner in his next life
note: Time to his first meal in a new life when he keeps what he learned, as a share of the time when it is wiped. Lower is better; the pass mark is half.

label: Short-term memory
note: How often the new ring memory recalls what it was shown, on five fresh runs. Tested on a bench: it holds the seat but is not yet wired into the living Jack.

label: Walking, against random flailing
note: How far the trained walker stands above a random one, in units of run-to-run spread. Measured in August on the old, large brain; the living Jack still rides a rover.

label: Learns a poison from one taste
note: After a single sub-lethal dose, how often he avoids that food next time. Tested on a bench in August, not in the living Jack.
